front_blocks.md: What is a **metal ore**?

back_blocks.md: A **metal ore** is a rock that contains enough metal (or metal compound) to make it economically worthwhile to extract the metal.

cards.front_md: What is a **metal ore**?
cards.back_md: A **metal ore** is a rock that contains enough metal (or metal compound) to make it economically worthwhile to extract the metal.

front_blocks.md: Why is the extraction of a metal from its oxide described as a reduction reaction?

back_blocks.md: Extraction from an oxide ore involves **removing oxygen** from the metal compound. Removal of oxygen is the definition of **reduction**, so the process is a reduction reaction.

cards.front_md: Why is the extraction of a metal from its oxide described as a reduction reaction?
cards.back_md: Extraction from an oxide ore involves **removing oxygen** from the metal compound. Removal of oxygen is the definition of **reduction**, so the process is a reduction reaction.

front_blocks.md: Metals **..........**  carbon in the reactivity series must be extracted by **..........**,  while metals **..........**  carbon can be extracted by heating with carbon or carbon monoxide.

back_blocks.md: Metals **above** carbon in the reactivity series must be extracted by **electrolysis**, while metals **below** carbon can be extracted by heating with carbon or carbon monoxide.

cards.front_md: Metals **..........**  carbon in the reactivity series must be extracted by **..........**,  while metals **..........**  carbon can be extracted by heating with carbon or carbon monoxide.
cards.back_md: Metals **above** carbon in the reactivity series must be extracted by **electrolysis**, while metals **below** carbon can be extracted by heating with carbon or carbon monoxide.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The higher a metal is in the reactivity series, the easier it is to extract from its ore.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

The **higher** a metal is in the reactivity series, the **more difficult** it is to extract. Highly reactive metals require electrolysis, which is expensive, while less reactive metals can be extracted more cheaply using carbon.

front_blocks.md: Why are gold and platinum sometimes found as uncombined elements in the Earth's crust?

back_blocks.md: Gold and platinum are very **unreactive** metals. Because they do not easily react with other substances, they are found as **native metals** — as pure, uncombined elements.

front_blocks.md: **Aluminium** is extracted from its ore by **..........**  because it is **..........**  carbon in the reactivity series.

back_blocks.md: Aluminium is extracted from its ore by **electrolysis** because it is **above** carbon in the reactivity series.

cards.back_md: Aluminium is extracted from its ore by **electrolysis** because it is **above** carbon in the reactivity series.

front_blocks.md: Why is electrolysis a more expensive extraction method than heating with carbon?

back_blocks.md: Electrolysis requires a **large amount of electricity**, which makes it costly. Heating with carbon uses fuel rather than electricity and is therefore cheaper.

**Iron** is below carbon in the reactivity series, so it can be extracted by **heating with carbon** (or carbon monoxide) in a blast furnace.

front_blocks.md: Why is the reduction of iron(III) oxide by carbon monoxide described as a reduction reaction?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: It is a **reduction** reaction because **oxygen is removed** from iron(III) oxide, leaving behind iron metal. Carbon monoxide acts as the **reducing agent**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Carbon monoxide is the main reducing agent in the blast furnace.
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Carbon monoxide** is formed when carbon (coke) reacts with carbon dioxide at high temperatures. It then reduces iron(III) oxide to produce **iron**, making it the main reducing agent.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of limestone in the blast furnace?
**(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **Limestone** (calcium carbonate) is added to remove acidic impurities in the ore. It thermally decomposes to form **calcium oxide**, which reacts with silicon dioxide impurities to form **slag** (calcium silicate).

front_blocks.md: What is **bauxite**?

back_blocks.md: **Bauxite** is the main ore of aluminium. It contains aluminium oxide, from which aluminium is extracted by electrolysis.

front_blocks.md: Why cannot aluminium be extracted from its ore using carbon?

back_blocks.md: Aluminium is **more reactive than carbon**, so carbon cannot displace it from its oxide. Only a more reactive substance can displace a less reactive one, so electrolysis is needed instead.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series.

back_blocks.md: **True.**

**Aluminium** is above carbon in the reactivity series. This means it cannot be extracted by reduction with carbon and must instead be extracted by the more energy-intensive process of **electrolysis**.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of molten cryolite in the extraction of aluminium?

back_blocks.md: **Cryolite** acts as a solvent, dissolving aluminium oxide so that it can conduct electricity and undergo **electrolysis**. It also lowers the melting point of the aluminium oxide, reducing energy costs.
